summary.suggested: The St. Louis Post-Dispatch's John E. Wray retold Tom Allen's 1869 fight with Mike McCoole, lost on an intimidated referee's decision, and his 1873 win over McCoole on Chouteau Island.

metadata.notes: St. Louis Post-Dispatch, Sunday Morning, March 30, 1941, page 14A.

facts.fact: Allen and McCoole first fought in 1869 on Foster's Island in the Mississippi near St. Louis; the ringside mob cut the ropes behind McCoole and threatened Allen with knives and guns
Referee Valentine McKinney ruled for McCoole that night at the Casino Theater, claiming Allen fouled by gouging an eye
Allen beat McCoole in seven rounds (16 minutes) on Chouteau Island, Sept. 23, 1873, for the world title when Tom Kelly threw in the towel; Allen was 33 years old and about 170 pounds
Allen covered $800 of McCoole's $1,000 bet and McCoole offered to lend him the other $200
Allen asked his handler Johnny Daly for a file and sharpened his spikes in his corner in front of McCoole
Allen shouted to Kelly: 'It's a shame to keep such a man before me. Take him out!'
facts.quote: It's a shame to keep such a man before me. Take him out!

facts.fact: Allen lost his title to Joe Goss three years later, at age 37
In his later years Allen was a retired proprietor of the Champion's Rest saloon

notes: Photo caption says Allen was 37 when he lost to Goss in 1876 and was a resident of St. Louis in 1873. Earlier record noted the article misdates his death; the held text does not.
